newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen consolidating in week ahead.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen consolidating in week ahead.

text.p: Brussels' Bel-20 share index which set yet another all-time high on Tuesday was seen by dealers consolidating in coming days, with market players taking a pause before investing further.
"I hope we'll stay above 2,000 for a week or so, but there's no reason for the market to collapse now," said trader Paul de Lophem at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
The Bel-20 .BFX leading shares index closed up 0.14 percent, or 2.83 points, at 2,024.97, with a moderate 2.5 billion francs volume of Belgian shares traded. It hit a new high of 2,028.92.
"It has become difficult to find good buying opportunities, everything is so high, and stocks which are not in the Bel-20 are also high, like Tessenderlo," De Lophem said.

Retailer GIB was the main bourse gainer, rising 3.64 percent to close at 1,565 francs after it said it was in talks to sell its Sarma deparment store group to a unit of NV Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer (KBB).
Dealers welcomed the announcement, saying they had been waiting two years for GIB to dump the unit.
The main bourse loser was non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere, closing down 1.76 percent to 2,230 francs.
Union Miniere failed to maintain last week's gains which were fuelled by higher zinc and dollar prices.
"Union Miniere is blocked at this level (2,240), the dollar and zinc prices are still good but from the fundamental point of view the company is not convincing," a trader said.
Dealers said focus was still on high quality stocks, like chemical and drug group UCB which offered a promising 1997. UCB closed unchanged at 93,500 francs.
Bank Delen analyst Gert De Mesure expected insurers Fortis AG and Royale Belge to perform well with bond yields down.
